elements.element: No non-compete restriction is imposed on Customer.
elements.evidence: Section 12.3 expressly states that nothing restricts Customer from developing, acquiring, licensing, selling, or using any product or service and confirms that Customer has made no non-compete commitment. Section 12.4 now grants permission rather than imposing a prohibition.

elements.element: No field-of-use restriction is imposed on Customer.
elements.evidence: Section 12.3 expressly permits Customer to conduct business in any field or territory. Section 12.4 contains no operative restriction.

elements.element: Any restriction is limited to a named competing product.
elements.evidence: No non-compete restriction remains, so there is no restriction requiring limitation to a named product. The reference in Section 12.4 to any competing product appears in an affirmative permission, not a prohibition.

elements.element: Any restriction applies during the term only and does not survive expiration or termination.
elements.evidence: No restriction exists during or after the term. Although Section 12.4's permission references the term and twenty-four months thereafter, Section 12.3 independently provides unrestricted rights without a time limit.

elements.element: Any restriction is capped at 12 months.
elements.evidence: No restriction exists, so the duration cap is not triggered. The twenty-four-month period in Section 12.4 qualifies an affirmative permission rather than a non-compete obligation.

elements.element: Any restriction includes a carve-out for Customer's internal development.
elements.evidence: Section 12.3 affirmatively provides that nothing restricts Customer from developing any product or service, and Section 12.4 also permits development of competing products or services.

elements.element: Any restriction includes a carve-out for acquisitions by Customer.
elements.evidence: Section 12.3 affirmatively provides that nothing restricts Customer from acquiring any product or service, and Section 12.4 also permits acquisition of competing products or services.

result.reason: The operative redline removes the non-compete by changing the prohibition in Section 12.4 into a permission, while Section 12.3 comprehensively confirms that Customer is unrestricted. It therefore satisfies the preferred position and, a fortiori, the fallback limitations. The change is minimal and does not alter unrelated commercial terms. Drafting quality is reduced because Section 12.4's time-limited permission is redundant and could invite an avoidable negative implication about the period after twenty-four months, notwithstanding Section 12.3's broader and unqualified protection.
